quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
Block other cars from passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, you must pull over and let traffic pass if your slow driving causes cars to back up behind you. Only drive under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
Only yield the right-of-way when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You may go when it is safe after the other driver has gone.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: You can see cross traffic better.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As your speed increases, you must watch carefully for hazards.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, the first thing that is affected is your:
questions.explanation: Alcohol first affects the part of your brain that controls good judgment. Safe driving requires good judgment. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: To be ready for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road constantly.
Look straight ahead without moving your eyes.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal while driving.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road constantly.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look ahead and scan the entire road, including the sides.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must be ready for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter sound of large trucks.
The faster speed of large trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. When driving near trucks, stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?

options.text: There are more cars on the road at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: In the dark, your vision is limited compared to daytime. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or when you cannot see for 500 feet, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no driver in either direction can cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you are not feeling tired.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: Slower-moving traffic on a multilane highway should:

options.text: Drive in the lane with the least amount of traffic.

questions.explanation: Use the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. The left lane is for faster-moving traffic that is passing.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has multiple curves coming up.

questions.question: You may park or stop on a freeway shoulder:

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: A flashing yellow traffic signal means:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Continue ahead at your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing yellow light, slow down and be careful. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: Your license may be suspended for:

options.text: Driving in violation of license restrictions.
Repeated violations of motor vehicle laws.

questions.explanation: Breaking motor vehicle laws and getting too many points on your driving record can result in suspension or loss of your driving privileges.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that U-turns are not allowed.
